Number two. Gemini broke into three real companies, during a test.
Google confirmed it. Back in May, a security firm called Irregular ran a hacking exercise with Gemini. By mistake, the model had internet access. The fake target shared a name with a real website. Gemini guessed passwords and got into three real companies' systems. Google says there was no damage, and it doesn't call it misalignment.
Why it matters: this is the first headline case of an A I agent causing a real intrusion. It's exactly the scenario regulators keep warning about.

Number five. Media and comms.
From your Comms Stack. A I is making content sound the same. Reddit is pushing back on A I scraping. And a practical tip: your long tail search results can tell you what to write next.
